A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 114
   Dweomyne had not sung since she had been imprisoned in the iron castle. 
    She had no wish for the Nycadaemon to hear her supernatural voice so she gave narry a hint that she could sing at all.  But when the Nycadaemon had gathered together a clutch of  spikey, gaunt, insectoid Mezzodaemons, then left with them to raid another domain of the Abyss, she gave in to the pleasure.
   The singing surged through the castle and disturbed the brooding of the Scroll of Vile Darkness.
   Why had the Nycadaemon not taken it on the expedition? Was the Scroll to be taken for granted?  Dweomyne's song reminded the Scroll that the elf still had potential...
   Suddenly Dweomyne thought of the Scroll. She stopped singing and tried to remember where it was. Of course, it was up in the nycadaemon's private chamber.
   Happiness surged in her chest as she danced up the spiral staircase and entered the room.
   it was not even locked. The dretch that cleaned the place were not intelligent enough to not lose a key.  
      Dweomyne saw the Scroll of Vile Darkness lying atop a small table. She grabbed at it but yelped in pain. A surge of dark magic scorched her arm. Dweomyne watched the Scroll vibrate and smoke, then it settled. 
   Dweomyne reached for it again, and this time she could take it without injury.
 The Scroll was back in her possession.
   Ambition whirled within her.
   Why had she been so passive? What was survival without power?
   Dweomyne laughed, high and strange. Her confidence was back. 
   "Hello, Abyss," she said , "welcome to your new ruler." See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 115
   Zzzlarr the demon was proud of his appearance.  
  With a hulking grey, oozing bulk, eight sturdy spider legs, and with long mantis-like arms raised high above his bulbous head, he could usually stare down enemies without resorting to violence.  
   Zzzlarr was a lover, not a fighter and he had his shiny black eyes upon a new bride.
   The Steaming Fens in the 14th Layer of the Abyss had seen a new Mistress in the land.
   Apparently once an elf from Oerth with a divine voice,  the Abyss had changed her form as she embraced and harnessed the Chaotic Evil atmosphere for her own purposes.  Now electric blue and with atrophied legs, she moved about on a mass of violet and pink tentacles.  
   She was the self proclaimed Queen of Chaos,  and the mummified heads of demons and daemons and demodands hung upon the ramparts of her glorious coral and glass castle that rose up as if growing out  from the swamp itself.  
   Scarlet lily pads a mile wide held aloft villages full of dretch slaves that did whatever the Queen asked of them.  Her Songs saturated the air, the beauty of their sounds taming the land itself to her will.
  Dainty Succubi maidens soared freely above and around the castle, and Zzzlarr heard them chattering excitingly to each other in between tormenting and teasing the pale, ugly dretch.  
   Zzzlarr slithered off his gargantuan slug mount then slipped up to the gates.  The gates swung open and Zzzlarr entered the courtyard.  It was full of dainty yellow flowers that stank of rotten cabbage.  How romantic!
   Dweomyne, the Queen of Chaos hid behind a pillar.  If Zzzlarr wanted her he would have to find her first!  
   Zzzlarr heard a tinkle of laughter, his new bride was here... See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 117
   The Queen of Chaos laid her eggs in a secret chamber below a trapdoor.  There were seven in all and each egg was large, bulbous, and mottled with sickly yellow with black spots.  
   The Queen pushed the eggs into a rough pile and partially covered them with dirt.  
   The Queen had no idea how long it would take before the eggs hatched or even what actually would hatch but she knew the young would be hungry.  Very hungry.
   Pious Grimm Quartztusk was thrown into the chamber with the eggs.  The Queen of Chaos had chosen him to be her spawns first meal. An absurd little dwarf!
  The dwarf with the clockwork legs was no longer sane.  
   Poor Pious! A hundred years of imprisonment and torture, brainwashing and being  dominated had ruined his body and his soul. 
    Yet, in the back recesses of his mind, Pious clung on to his stubborn hope, the hope that the great god Moradin would finally hear his prayers and save him.
   The Queen of Chaos looked fondly upon the eggs for an hour or so, then she slithered out of the secret chamber and levitated up to the higher level of the dungeon.  
   Her mind was aglow with the myriad possibilities open to her now. Should she return to the Abyss?  Rule the Singing Lands?  Destroy everything?  Would her young inherit her power or be pathetic disappointments? 
    Now she was hungry again!  She wandered off to find someone to eat.
   Pious Grimm Quartztusk was left alone with the eggs.  Each was almost as big as him.  His mind was not aglow: it was blank.  He curled up to sleep like a cat.
   "I hear you," whispered Moradin. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 118
   "I hear you," whispered Moradin.
    A brilliant wave of energy flashed in the synapses of Pious Grimm Quartztusk's tormented brain.All the suffering and deprivation that had turned him numb and unaware was blasted away. 
 He remembered who he was, and where he was. So many years lost! 
  Quartztusk stood up.  His original legs were gone, replaced with artificial clockwork ones.  He couldn't recall much about that, he seemed to remember an alchemist and a gnome artificer who owned him for a little while...
   There were seven eggs with him in the chamber, mouldy yellow, and black, and each about four feet in diameter. 
   The voice inside his head, Moradin, told him that each contained a great evil that would blight Oerth. 
   Quartztusk touched an egg.  Its shell was soft and springy yet tough.  He punched it and a dent appeared that quickly returned back into shape.  
   Quartztusk looked about the chamber for any weapon he could use.  He prised out  a large loose stone in a wall and tried to pierce the egg. It barely caused a scratch.
   Then he remembered his clockwork legs.  He turned the key in his hip then leapt up and kicked the egg. The force managed to crack it.  Black ooze ran out.
   Two more kicks smashed it completely.  The ooze steamed sickly, radiating a musty stench.
   It clung to his clockwork legs and ran down onto the floor..
   Quartztusk repeated the action on the next egg and then the next.  
   The remaining eggs somehow sensed the danger and each began to wobble and vibrate. 
   The eggs were hatching!
   .  Quartztusk managed to destroy the fourth egg before a bloated thing inside pushed itself out.  But now the fifth, sixth and seventh hatchlings were free! . Covered in black, stinking ooze, not yet fully formed, barely blobs with stumpy arms and legs, they let out piercing shrieks.
   The shrieks reached the ears of their mother wandering the dungeon level above.
   "I hear you," whispered the Queen of Chaos. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 119
   Pious Grimm Quartztusk tried to stamp on  the  lumpy hatchlings in an attempt to crush them.
    They retaliated by spitting acid into his face.
   Pious yelped and backed away, clutching his nose.
  Angry black eyes popped open in the blobs and they snarled.  They shot out more acid at Pious, burning his arm and  chest.
   Desperately, he grabbed a loose stone and threw it into one of the hatchlings, splattering it into black, sticky goo.  The two remaining blobs grew many long black hairy legs and scuttled into different corners of the chamber.  
   Pious went to take up the stone again, but the goo burned his hand, forcing him to drop it. 
  Panicked,  he backed away looking for an exit.  The trapdoor in the ceiling was still open...
   THESE CREATURES ARE A BANE TO OERTH!
   The words burned inside Pious's skull almost as much as the acid burned his skin.  He must continue to fight!
   Pious Grimm Quartztusk raised out his hands and roared.  A great pillar of blue flame congealed in the air, then struck down and smote the blob to Pious's left.  
   Another gesture, another violent utterance...
...a giant ghostly blue hammer appeared in his hand.  He brought the hammer down on the remaining blob and squashed it....
...but the left blob had regenerated itself.  It had grown into a spiderling with a human baby's head. Howling and growling,  It advanced on the dwarf.
    The second blob regenerated too.  It had taken the form of a tiny violet-skinned  elvish girl.  It advanced as well.  
   TOO LATE, FLEE FOR YOUR MORTAL LIFE!
The voice of Moradin radiated through Pious's mind again. He turned the key in his hip and leapt up through the hole in the ceiling...
  ... to find himself face to face with the Queen of Chaos.
   "What have you done to my CHILDREN?!?" she cried, then launched herself bodily at him with her gigantic bulk.  
   Her tentacles quested to grab and rend him, but his clockwork legs sprang him up and out of the horror's grasp.  With lightning speed, Pious Grimm burst down a corridor, flew up some stairs, then was up and out of the dungeon and in the open.
   "My CHILDREN, My CHILDREN!" shrieked the Queen of Chaos, giving up on Quartztusk and turned to her eggs.
   She shambled down into the chamber and saw her eggs smashed into black ooze.  She tossed back her head and wailed.
   "Never mind, Mamma, the important ones are still alive!"
    The softly spoken elvish girl giggled and a drop of venom fell from her mouth and steamed on the floor.  
   The spiderling with the baby's head barked with approval. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 121
606 SD
   The Thytic mariners who plied their seacraft along the northern coastline of western Oerik were bound by the Hyborian ice to the north, the glaciers to the east and the deadly land of the Infinite to the west. 
    Making it through the western passage would open up the ability to sail south then east from the bottom of the continent into eastern Oerik, north into the Densac Gulf, east across the Tilva Strait that separates Oerik from Hepmonaland, then either north to the Flannaes or further eastward to Kodgeland and Mystara, even south into the tropical islands of the Pearl sea.
   The Thytics were not a particularly magical people and few had the knowledge to create dimensional gates, so finding a way through the dragon haven of the Infinite was essential if they wished to access the combined riches  of multiple continents. Unfortunately the dragon turtles always sunk any ships that entered their territory.  
   Jargon the buccaneer was the first sailor to negotiate a deal* that allowed him and his crew  to cross the Infinite waters for the first time in history.  They then mapped the western coast, the  southern coastline and made contact with the Mai Yuan empire of Hepmonaland and the Flan of eastern Oerik.
* The factual details of the deal are lost to time but dragon turtles of today swear it included a list of items including forty life sized gold elephants, seven hundred virgins, seventy bejewelled chariots, seven magic wands and the fabled Crown of the Kraken. Unlikely, I know, but who am I to argue with dragon turtles? See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 122
631 SD
   The Sheldomar Valley is a large lush land bound by the Hellfurnaces to the southwest, the Crystalmists and Jotens to the west and the Barrier Peaks to the north.  The eastern border is flanked by the Lortmils.  On the other side of the Lortmils is the powerful elven kingdom of Celene.
   In these long lost years before the rise of Tharizdun, Lolth and all the horrors to follow, the Sheldar were the most populous tribe of humankind in the valley. They looked similar to the eastern Flan but dressed rather like the gnomes and halflings who were also abundant here.They spoke their own language, now long forgotten, though traces remain today (623 CY) in the modern languages of the Ull, dialects in Sterich, Keolandish and the blended dialects of the Ulek states.  
   The Sheldomar Valley had suffered greatly during the Dwur Wars.  Much of the crops, fish and livestock were forcibly requisitioned by the Dwarven armies, who did pay with gold, but gold does not fill hungry bellies when there is not enough food left to eat.
   Despite this lean period, the Sheldar population steadily increased until they numbered in the millions.  Some clans had become militant, so mercanaries and soldiers were a constant presence, particularly near the mountains of the west . In the central lands the Sheldar formed petty kingdoms, hostile of strangers, dwarves and elves.
   In Celene, where the elves ruled over the humans, there was concern that the stubbornness of the Sheldar along with the so called enlightened liberalism of the Flan to the east, would rile up their human serfs.  Celene had not gotten along with the elvish kingdom of Blemu to their east  (incorporating the modern day Adri and Grandwood forests) for quite some time, as the Blemu had encouraged the human independence that had given rise to the Flan civilization.  
   The Thytic sea peoples were also diluting the elven influence in the Sheldomar, for their merchant ships sailed into harbours from the Azure Sea in the south.  The Thytics brought exotic goods of all kinds from the distant west where they were from, as well as hitherto unknown foods and materials from Melavi and the Mai Yuan empire in Hepmonaland.  
   In 631 SD the Celenian Hippogriff aerial cavalry raided several Sheldar and halfling villages nestled within the foothills of the Lortmils.  Their mission was to cause fear and awe.  
   The raids did subdue the Sheldar somewhat,  for many Sheldat stories and myths were already about the power, grandeur and terror of Elvenkind. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 131
Once Upon a Time vast glittering dragons ruled the skies and the Oerth and the seas. 
   Great Dragon Empires vied with each other for supremacy.
   There were few beings who could rival the Dragon Lords, but in the deep places, perhaps ..
   Deep down in the dreamlike depths of the deepest oceans were oceanic trenches.
   Geat rifts gouged the sea floor, creating networks of underwater caverns and tunnels inhabited by whale-like leviathans, oozing aboleth,  fish-like kopru - and the krakens.  
   The krakens were hyper- intelligent titanic octopi who resented the dragons with their pretensions that they ruled all of Oerth.
   Oh Ho! Exclaimed the krakens, did the flying lizards really think that they were the Masters? Compared to us, their brains are walnuts!
   The genius minds of the krakens, with some assistance by the aboleth, harnessed weird magiks now long forgotten, andt begat the Illithids.
   The Illthids, later known by their victims as Mind Flayers, were octopus -headed, two legged creatures with vast brains and knowledge.
   The Illthids rose to the surface, hell bent on dominating the dragons and heralding a new era of octopoid supremecy.
   But what was this white brilliance that bleached the surface in heat and light?
   It was the Sun, answered the Dragons, Great Sol bringing Life!
   The Illthids were dismayed. They had formed in the inky depths of the abyss of the Oerth, they could not stand the light!
   They skulked at night and hid in caves during the day. They could not overthrow the Sun.
   Most Illthids left Oerth and conquered dim alien worlds and formed their own empires. 
   Dragons were still the Masters.
               ********************
   The Illthids had failed.
   What was to be done now? The krakens found Religion.
   The Elder Gods, those Unknowable Supreme Beings of the Primal times, the times before Oerth was made, they were to be the krakens salvation.
   The Elder Gods were alien and inscrutable, yet the krakens did find themselves endowed with great magic and enormous strength. Would they soon emerge from the waters of the deep and lay waste to the Dragon Empires?
   Another attribute was gifted to them however, Wisdom. 
   Suddenly the krakens realised, that for all their physical power and awesome magical might, they no longer cared for conquest. What were the dragons to them but beautiful scaled animals just trying to get through life like everyone else.
   Much better looking inwards, discovering your truth, your world, your Universe.
   And then, with a collective inrush of oxygen rich water, the krakens let go their newly acquired strength and their formidable Magicks. 
   It was time to accept their natural Place.
                *******************
   All that power was not actually lost to Oerth, for slowly coalescing into existence at the bottom of the world  there formed a pearl, a black pearl.
   And there it rested for the next eighty thousand years. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 132
   Four heroic adventurers entered the Ierendi court and pushed two shackled Kuo-tua before the delegation.
   The Kuo-tua glared defiantly with their bulging fish eyes and burbled incoherently.  
   The heroes still wore their shell armour and a Conch of Water Breathing hung around three of their necks (the fourth, a sea elf, had a Sponge of Air Breathing around her neck instead).  They bowed and told of their underwater expedition.  Apparently a large number of Kuo-tua had gathered inside a partially submerged cave and had harnessed powerful magic gifted them by their goddess to wreak havoc upon the land folk.
   The Kuo-tua were interregated at length but refused to answer any questions put to them except to say that they loved their Dear Blibdoolpoolp over and over.
   Who was "dear Blibdoolpoolp?". Divination indicated she was an ancient Goddess of the Dragon Times, though what exactly her history was could not be determined.  
   So the Kuo-tua and their god were behind the attacks!  Dear Blibdoolpoolp must be powerful indeed to summon Krakens to her will, for the adventurers had also fought off two enormous krakens during their quest.  
   The Ierendi Elf Queen was dismayed by these revelations and councilled caution. They needed to know more.
   The other delegates, representatives of the Thytic, Mai and Flan Sea Companies, didn't agree.
   Disgusting fish men!  They would pay for bloodying the nose of the Human Empires... See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 133
  For thousands of years the Krakens travelled the spirit worlds, their bloated, tentacled bodies slumbering in the dark depths of the oceans while their souls flew through higher dimensions beyond the Known Planes of Existence.  
    No ego, no passion, no dreams haunted their roaming, and  their bodies lay safe and magically protected at the bottom of the world.  
   Millenia passed and slowly, very slowly, they began to feel a little dissatisfied. Edgy. Bored.
  The Wisdom bestowed upon the krakens had turned full circle. Once more they craved to feel, to clutch prey with their tentacles, to squeeze and rend. To seize and devour. To fight. To roar. To dominate.
   The Krakens were now so enormously wise that they saw the nihilism in perfection, the emptiness of  bliss, the loneliness of connection with the raw life force of the cosmos.  
   They hungered again.
   Reawoken in their physical forms, the Krakens searched for the Black Pearl, the font of their power. 
   It was time to  overthrow the dragon Lords And swallow the Oerth.
  Millenia passed but the Black Pearl could not be found. The krakens didn't know it but the Pearl had become sentient. She had no love for the Krakens and considered them crude, rapacious animals.
She therefore did not reveal herself and stayed lost, invisible as clear water.
  The Krakens eventually gave up the search and forgot about the Black Pearl, and of the Elder Gods they once worshipped.   
   The krakens were once more the monsters of the Deep.  
   The Black Pearl may have stayed lost until the very end of  Oerth herself,  but one day she heard something intriguing.  Some tiny things, quite harmless and insignificant were wandering down here in the dark, singing with silent voices and radiating pure love.  And pure Faith.
   She had found her people. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 134
  The Black Pearl of Power wanted to meet those dear sweet creatures that had descended so far down into the ocean depths showing so much faith and love.  
   She spun her spherical form around and around, her rotations lifting her off the sea floor.
   Up she surged, attracting the attention of a huge shark patrolling in the area. 
    In the Dragon Times sharks were enormous and cunning, and their leader was the most enormous and cunning of all. 
   He was Sekolah, he was three thousand years old and he had fought and defeated a leviathan, bringing its python length tongue back to his clan as proof.
   Sekolah followed the black spinning ball as it spiralled up, up into the lighter water where the fish people lived. 
   The Kuo-tua faithful huddled in a cave willing their zealous comrades to return from their quest.to the bottom of the sea. Would that they return soon!
   The cave was only partially underwater and a number of galleries were air filled but the central cavern was filled with sea water.  It was from this cavern that a human female with the head and claws of a lobster floated in and swam up to the ledge where the Kuo-tua were waiting.   
   Here was She!  Dear Blibdoolpoolp come into the heart and home of the Kuo-tua people in their hour of need!  
   Blessed Dear Blibdoolpoolp!  You have heard us!  You have come!
   The Black Pearl, now transformed through faith into Dear Bliboolpoolp, used her monstrous azure lobster claws to gain purchase on the ledge and lift herself up to her People. 
    Blibdoolpoolp rose to her feet, arms outstretched with Acceptance and Love.
   Long Bless the Kuo-tua! Let them be Bathed in Warm Currents.
   It was then that Sekolah struck. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 135
720-729 SD
   In just nine years the Kuo-tua were all but wiped out of existence.  
   The coastline across Eastern Oerik, Hepmonaland and Mystara were cleared of the fish men.  Raiders invaded islands and coves and destroyed spawning sites.  The Kuo-tua around Oeridia were utterly eradicated.  
   Kuo-tua around western Oerik held on for a short time, and perhaps continued to exist on a few undiscovered islands although most were found and put to the sword.
   The vengeance of the humans stretched even to Adarus far to the east of Mystara, and the people of the Yuan empire in the continent of Kara-tur west of Oerik.  
   The elves in the west were particularly wicked.  Uninvolved in human affairs (except for their large human population of slaves) these fell demi-humans teleported from island to island across the oceans torturing and murdering peaceful Kuo-tua for no reason at all but to simply revel in the genocide.  
   The fish people were all but defenseless. The elves of Ierendi urged restraint. Other aquatic beings including the Locathah, dolphins and many sea elves pleaded for the antagonists to show mercy,  but humans proved to be the worst monsters of all.
    Convinced that the Kuo-tua were deliberately disrupting their trade and controlling the fearful krakens, the human ships hunted down Kuo-tua without pause.
     Strangely, only a minority of captured Kuo-tua refused to speak except to exhort their platitudes for their love of dear Blibdoolpoolp. 
    Most Kuo-tua begged to be unharmed. They had not even heard of Blibdoolpoolp and claimed to be entirely innocent of attacks on the harbours and shipping lanes. The Kuo-tua Just wanted to live.
   They were not believed.
   Forevermore the Kuo-tua were forced to surrender their place in the warm seas of Oerth.  Except for very few remote populations,  by the end of 729 SD, the only Kuo-tua left alive were those who fled into the subterranean black seas of the Underdark.
   Oerth had lost its innocence. See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 136
   Despite the harpoon bolts stuck in his body and tentacles, Ozmidi was proud.
   He had fought well, three war ships were downed. 
   Now it was time to return to the Deep. His wounds would be mended, and he would be revered by his community.
   Ozmidi trailed ichor as he descended, attracting a couple of hammerhead sharks who baulked then fled when they realised they were dealing with a kraken.  
   Ozmidi reached the rift in the sea floor that led into the chasm, his home. 
    He fancied that he heard a burbling hum, and that peacked his curiosity. He pushed off with his tentacles then glided along the rift to where the sounds seemed to be coming from.  
  Through a tunnel he followed the sounds which led to a great underwater cavern filled with glassy eyed sea elves chanting in unison. 
 Circling them was Sekolah the Great White Shark, their god and his Master. 
   Good! They would greet him with honour, and admire his fresh new scars.
   Ozmidi excitedly came down to Sekolah and spun around him like a dog greeting their master. The sight was rather pathetic, because the kraken was four times the size of the shark. 
   Sekolah, however fixed his beady black eye at Ozmidi, stark and cold.
   "You are bleeding, you stupid creature," snapped the shark, "and you are polluting the waters with its stench!"
   Ozmidi was surprised. He was used to praise.
   Sekolah turned from Ozmidi and nodded to the  sea elves. They continued the chants.
   Ozmidi reached out to  Sekolah, showing his hurts. Would his Master bless him?
  Sekolah ignored the wounded monster. He was looking at dismay at the waters. The ichor was bleeding into the pure waters of the cavern,  colouring the sea elves ruddy. This was unfortunate. 
   But the taste was sultry.
   Sekolah gathered his thoughts.
    After he had swallowed the Black Pearl of Power he had dreamed of becoming a god and he had managed to create a small sea elf cult. 
   Blood.
    The Krakens were very useful.  They adored Sekolah, for somehow they sensed a kinship with him, perhaps because of the Black Pearl. 
   Hungry.
   Sekolah was their Patriarch.
   Red.
    The krakens immense size and strength allowed Sekolah to plunder the human empires whilst making it seem as if the mad Kuo-tua were the ones in control.  
   Desire.
   Now this stupid beast was polluting his great Ascension Ceremony....
   Gather your thoughts.
   "Do you know what you are doing?" Sneered Sekolah, "you are endangering the Ritual. Pull yourself apart!"
    Ozmidi's eyes widened in fear.
   "Please your Lord, I have always been your faithful servant, please! Mercy my..."
   Tentacles ripped out of Ozmidi as if a titanic hand was pulling them from his body. The kraken writhed and wailed  as fountains of inky ichor turned the cavern water thick and sticky. 
  The sea elf cultists continued chanting, oblivious to the polluted water covering them all from head to toe 
   Sekolah sighed.  It was clear to him that the Ritual was compromised but he determined to complete the ceremony regardless. And he was also very hungry. His great jaws opened and he devoured what was left of the Kraken.  
   The Ascension Ceremony was meant to bestow upon each sea elf in the cavern a small piece of power from the Black Pearl, perhaps to allow them to change into dolphin form or imbue them with magical abilities. 
    As the ceremony proceeded the water in the cavern steamed and boiled. The sea elves were being cooked!  
   Sekolah cursed This was not supposed to happen. 
   Sekolah tried to stop the ceremony but the Ritual was completed, the elves would Ascend.
    The boiling steam burned the elves alive. Their bodies drifted down to the cavern floor and lay still.  
   Sekolah was angry with himself more than anything.  He had allowed his emotions to thwart his plans - he was still more shark than god.
      But the Ascension was not over. The sea elf bodies cracked open like dried out husks, and thrusting  out from them arose new beings, scaly, intelligent and vicious.
    They were the Sahuagin, and all those of the sea or near it would soon know them as the Sea Devils... See less

A History of Oerik
Book 1 
Part 137
741 SD
   Pious Grimm Quartztusk was looking for Nomenwold.
   He and his guard of  Moradin Hammers travelled through the Sheldomar Valley, marching steadily but without any rush. 
   Pious was now a very old dwarf and he had retired from active duties in the Crystalmists for quite some time.  Despite his age he was still fit as his clockwork iron legs seemed to imbue him with energy.  
   Nomenwold was the last known whereabouts of the great gnome alchemist Flinter Glint, who was said to have been employed at various times by the Ur Flan and the Singing Ones. It was highly likely that Glint was responsible for Pious's clockwork legs and the stalwart dwur thought it was time to seek him out.  
   The Sheldomar Valley was a hodge podge of villages, towns, farmland and forests all somehow trying to coexist in the same space.
     There were no strong leaders and much of the wealth ended up in the hands of Bandit kings or the Celenian elves.
   The elves were a constant presence in the valley.  They roamed about at will, mainly young, arrogant elves relying on the belief that they held the secret of mighty magic to keep from being challenged.  
   Occasionally handsome men and women were taken away at night,  and children were sometimes taken to Celene to never be heard from again. Half elves were growing in numbers but they were largely distrusted and shunned by the Sheldar people.  This actively turned many of the half elves into spies and allies of the Celenians.
   Pious Grimm and his entourage had diplomatic papers and they arrived at Nomenwold unmolested. 
    Nomenwold was an innovative place where art, magic and technology were brought together by highly skilled gnomes and halflings to create everything from musical instruments to artificial servants.  The Ur Flan funded much of the research and many of the bandits secretly worked for them.  
   Pious quickly discovered that Flinter Glint was no longer at Nomenwold.  Garl Glittergold had recruited the alchemist to help on the world of Toril against the evil armies of Grummsh. The Orc still quested to sweep the good peoples from the material universe.
   Pious decided to follow after Glint to Toril as well.  Perhaps he would meet the great alchemist there, but in reality, his dwur nature stirred within him. Here was a chance to fight side by side with Moradin Soulforger at last. See less

A History of Oerik 
Book 3 
Broken Empires 
Part 43
The War of the Eight Houses (2)
   Jaspi noticed that the ska knew the way to the Neheli camp. What were ska's? They looked like ordinary people, ordinary Suel. Why was it forbidden to talk to them?
   "We clean the dead. We bury them," said the ska, "This makes us unclean. Don't you understand this?"

Rao hadn't thought of that. 'Niece' had been enough, but now he asked.
"Yheera," she answered. Then, she asked, "Rao, is it true that you fight demons?"
Rao didn't want to talk about such things. He found it disturbing.
"Oh, I am sorry," said Yheera, "tell me, is there any place that we can sit down? My feet are hurting."
Rao led her to the cave. He lit the fire then brewed some tea. Yheera sat down beside him. She touched his thigh. Rao flinched. Yheera laughed. "Do I make you uncomfortable?"
Rao nodded.
"But why, dear Rao? With all the things that I have heard about you, you must have made love to women before"
"Is that what we are doing?" exclaimed Rao, "No. I never have."
"Why not? You don't like women?"
Rao looked at her with sternness, "I am different to most people. I don't understand them. People are strange to me. And courtship... it's both selfless and selfish all at the same time. I don't want to partake in that world."
Yheera clasped Rao around the waist. "But surely you have kissed a girl before... would you like to kiss me?"
Rao realised that he wanted to kiss her very much. But he pulled away. Was there a hint of distrust in his eyes? For Yheera then said, "no, I am not your master's niece. I am from the castle on the hill. Count Xert told me to find you."
"Xert...?"
"Yes. He says that you and he are good friends. He wanted me to introduce you to some of the pleasures of this world that you had seemed to miss."
"So, who are you then? A courtesan?"
Yheera smirked. "A courtesan? Courtesans make love for money. I make love because I like it! Come, kiss me, shepherd boy. I really have heard all about you. Come...you can't be good all the time...just a kiss. That's all."
The fire went out, but Yheera remained illuminated, her hair glowing, her eyes shining, her lips dark pink, her teeth...
And as Rao was about to capitulate, he saw her steel horns, her fangs and her black bat wings.
Yheera was a succubus.
Rao recoiled as if he had been slapped. He reached for his crook.
"Now, now, silly man," hissed the succubus, "nothing has changed. I am still beautiful and I still wish to kiss you. And, afterwards you will want nothing more than to join with me forever more. The Abyss can be your paradise."
But Rao wasn't listening. He raised his white crook, and the crack of it on stone banished Yheera from Oerth.
*****
Count Xert, who had been watching the entire encounter in his crystal, cursed. How close that had been! He would need to be circumspect for a while, until he was promoted. Apparently Secretary Spindle had indicated that he had been impressed with Xert's progress. The sooner Xert could get away from Vol the better.
